page: Google Cloud Platform n4-highcpu-16 is a compute-focused instance configuration within the N4 virtual machine family. Powered by dedicated Intel x86_64 processors, this instance provides 16 virtual CPUs derived from 8 physical cores via multithreading. It features 32 GB of system memory, yielding a 2 GB per vCPU ratio suitable for CPU-heavy tasks. Cache resources include 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large 260 MB L3 cache pool. The underlying silicon includes advanced vector and matrix acceleration instructions such as AVX-512, AMX-TILE, and AMX-INT8, alongside cryptographic hardware extensions like VAES and SHA-NI.

Hardware metrics show consistent mid-tier execution throughput. The system delivered a single-core Geekbench score of 1886.0 and a multi-core score of 11411.0, while Passmark registered an overall CPU score of 21470.49. In synthetic compute benchmarks, stress-ng produced 1781.09 operations single-core and 14630.37 multi-core. In memory bandwidth evaluations, the instance handled small cached reads at 1133.53 GB/sec, large uncached reads at 130.97 GB/sec, and writes at 72.76 GB/sec. Application testing yielded 17.79 million Redis SET operations per second and 25.59 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

The configuration carries specific architectural tradeoffs. With no integrated local storage disks, persistent root and data volumes must be provisioned via external networked storage options. Similarly, the server lacks dedicated discrete GPU accelerators, relying entirely on the Intel host CPU for mathematical execution. While matrix engines support inference for small language models, achieving 261.82 tokens per second on 135M parameter models and 11.2 tokens per second on 7B models, it cannot process larger 70B models due to the 32 GB memory ceiling.

This server type delivers cost efficiency by allocating compute cores with a moderate memory footprint, avoiding unnecessary memory overhead for non-data-dense applications. Recommended workloads include distributed continuous integration, software build pipelines, batch data processing, API endpoints, web microservices, and general compute tasks that require dedicated thread scheduling without heavy RAM requirements.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4-highcpu-16 is a compute-oriented virtual machine designed for processor-heavy enterprise workloads. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical Intel x86_64 cores and 32 GB of system memory, matching a 2 GB per vCPU allocation. The processor features hardware acceleration engines including AVX-512 and AMX for matrix math, alongside a 260 MB L3 cache. In performance testing, the instance posted a Passmark CPU score of 21470.49 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 11411.0, while demonstrating high memory bandwidth with 130.97 GB/sec large-block uncached reads. The server includes no bundled local storage disks or hardware GPUs, necessitating network storage for data persistence. Delivering balanced throughput for CPU-bound pipelines without paying for surplus memory, the n4-highcpu-16 is suited for continuous integration build systems, media encoding, static web servers, and distributed data transformation jobs.
